audit_scope: 6 target adapters + scan for other stubs across the full 316-line file

routing_context.authority_switch: m6_authority_route (authority.py L387-461). When FW_CONTEXT_M6_READ_AUTHORITY=1 (DEFAULT per m6_read_authority_enabled, authority.py L464-470), production reads route to the m6_* adapter. When disabled, the legacy_fn (the pre-M7 baseline) is called.
routing_context.pre_m7_baseline: For each tool, legacy_fn passed to m6_authority_route. Two shapes: (a) direct legacy handler for get_vector_table (callgraph.get_vector_table) and compare_variants (variants.compare_variants); (b) v2_authority_route(legacy_handler, v2_shadow_adapter) for trace_data_flow, get_method_overrides, get_template_instances, explain_condition — i.e. v2 shadow adapter first, legacy handler fallback.
routing_context.m6_query_backing: Confirmed: m6_query.py defines real query primitives for ONLY lookup_symbol, search_code, find_callers, find_references, get_symbol_context, get_class_members, search_bodies, get_file_map, get_source. NONE of the 6 target adapters (nor the other stubs listed below) have a backing m6_query primitive — they all return hardcoded values.

target_adapters.m6_returns: [{"info": "vector table not available in M6 store"}]  — hardcoded, never touches the M6 store.
target_adapters.pre_m7_behavior: Legacy handler callgraph.get_vector_table (callgraph.py L2417) via _vector_rows (L2305-2414). Real implementation: reads interrupt vector table from THREE sources — index_db.get_vector_table (assembly address words + C arrays), build artifact registrations (read_isr_registrations), and the linked ELF image (_from_the_elf). Adds coverage trailers and an interrupt-connected/unserviced summary. Documented 'never empty: one dict with info' contract. No v2 shadow adapter exists for this tool (routed direct: m6_authority_route('get_vector_table', callgraph.get_vector_table, m6_get_vector_table), server.py L1277).
target_adapters.detail: Returns a hardcoded 'info' dict shaped exactly like the legacy 'no vector table in this build' empty-result contract. A caller checking the `info` key cannot distinguish 'this build genuinely has no vector table' from 'the M6 adapter is a stub that never looked'. The message names 'M6 store' which is a mild hint, but the return is presented in the legitimate empty-result shape. All three real data sources (index, artifact, ELF) and the coverage/interrupt summary are lost.

target_adapters.m6_returns: {"name": method_name, "overrides": [], "overridden_by": []}  — hardcoded, never touches the M6 store.
target_adapters.pre_m7_behavior: Two-layer v2_authority_route (server.py L1374-1377): v2_shadow_get_method_overrides (v2_shadow_adapters.py L3458-3681) first — real v2 read that derives the override relation from inherit edges + USR-shape heuristics (strips @F@ suffix to find enclosing class, walks base/derived classes, looks up same-named methods). Falls back to legacy inheritance.get_method_overrides (inheritance.py L501-594) — reads the post-process `overrides` table via get_overrides_for_method and returns real overrides/overridden_by lists with usr/name/qualified_name/kind/file/line.
target_adapters.detail: Returns the SUCCESS shape ({name, overrides, overridden_by}) with both lists hardcoded empty. This is indistinguishable from a legitimate 'this method has no overrides and is overridden by nothing' result. A caller has no way to detect that the M6 adapter never queried the store. Both v2 and legacy baselines return real override data; the M6 stub returns empty lists unconditionally regardless of input.

target_adapters.m6_returns: []  — hardcoded empty list, never touches the M6 store.
target_adapters.pre_m7_behavior: Two-layer v2_authority_route (server.py L1380-1383): v2_shadow_get_template_instances (v2_shadow_adapters.py L3684-3860) first — real v2 read using a name + USR-shape heuristic over semantic_symbols_core (finds is_template=1 pattern, builds USR set {primary + partial specs}, scans is_template=0 rows whose USR carries template-arg markers). Falls back to legacy inheritance.get_template_instances (inheritance.py L368-498) — reads the `template_usr` column populated by the T09 instance-discovery pass (ADR-007), resolves partial-spec USR set, returns template declaration + instances[] + instance_count.
target_adapters.detail: Returns [] which the legacy contract explicitly defines as 'No match gives []' (inheritance.py L427). A caller therefore concludes 'no template by that name / no instances' when in fact the M6 adapter never queried the store. This is the most dangerous silent degradation: the empty list is the documented not-found answer, so callers will silently miss real template instantiations. The template declaration row, instance list, instance_count, and partial-spec resolution are all lost.

target_adapters.m6_returns: [{"info": "data flow tracing requires call graph analysis"}]  — hardcoded, never touches the M6 store. Ignores type_name and to_symbol.
target_adapters.pre_m7_behavior: Two-layer v2_authority_route (server.py L1326-1329): v2_shadow_trace_data_flow (v2_shadow_adapters.py L1476-1607) first — real v2 read: LIKE-scans semantic_symbols_core.signature for type_name, resolves target USRs via v2_lookup_symbol, builds call-graph adjacency over call/indirect/fp_assign edges, runs BFS shortest paths per source, returns _summary + per-source entries (source_name/kind/file/line, caller_count, reachable, paths). Falls back to legacy callgraph.trace_data_flow (callgraph.py L1758-1918) — reads symbols table for signature LIKE matches ranked by caller_count, calls index_db.find_call_path BFS per source with per-iteration timeout_ms guard and timed_out markers.
target_adapters.detail: Returns an 'info' dict — the legacy 'Never empty: one dict with info replaces an empty result' shape (callgraph.py L1817). A caller checking for the `info` key treats this as 'no data flows found', when really the M6 adapter never ran. The info message ('requires call graph analysis') is a mild hint but is presented in the legitimate empty-result shape, so callers cannot programmatically distinguish stub from genuine no-result. All source-function discovery, BFS path tracing, caller_count ranking, reachable/paths, and timeout handling are lost.

target_adapters.m6_returns: {"file": file_path, "line": line, "chain": []}  — hardcoded, never touches the M6 store.
target_adapters.pre_m7_behavior: Two-layer v2_authority_route (server.py L1395-1398): v2_shadow_explain_condition (v2_shadow_adapters.py L4097-4217) first — real v2 read: resolves file blob via binding_file_map, reads semantic_condition_index root regions + branch rows, annotates with tu_branch_states, returns chain with directive/condition/branch_states (documented M3B limitation: no line numbers so no line-enclosure filtering — returns ALL root groups). Falls back to legacy conditionals.explain_condition (conditionals.py L31-168) — reads conditionals/conditional_branches/conditional_macros tables, performs proper line-enclosure filtering (root.line <= line <= end_line), returns chain with branch_states (taken 1/0/-1) and macro_inputs (with def_source/def_file/def_line).
target_adapters.detail: Returns {file, line, chain: []}. The legacy contract explicitly states 'A file with no conditional directives returns chain: []' and 'A line outside every conditional group gives an empty chain' (conditionals.py L67, L71). The M6 stub therefore looks identical to a legitimate 'this line is not enclosed by any #ifdef' answer. A caller has no way to detect that the M6 adapter never queried the conditional index. All conditional-chain data, branch_states, macro_inputs, line-enclosure filtering, and context_id/config_hash provenance are lost.

target_adapters.m6_returns: {"a": a, "b": b, "kind": "build", "error": "variant comparison not yet implemented in M6"}  — hardcoded, never touches the M6 store.
target_adapters.pre_m7_behavior: Legacy handler variants.compare_variants (variants.py L477-596+) via direct routing (server.py L1412: m6_authority_route('compare_variants', variants.compare_variants, m6_compare_variants), NO v2 shadow). Real implementation: resolves both builds by variant label, supports symbol/file/build modes, compares across dimensions (existence, signature, body_fingerprint, edges with call-site certainty, conditions with branch states, defines with deltas), every fact carries provenance (variant/image/config_hash).
target_adapters.detail: LEAST silently degraded of the six: the return includes an explicit `error` key with the honest message 'variant comparison not yet implemented in M6'. The legacy contract says 'On failure the dict holds only error with the reason' (variants.py L551), so a caller checking for `error` WILL see the limitation. However it is not functionally equivalent (no comparison is performed, all dimensions/provenance are lost) and the shape is mixed (error alongside a/b/kind rather than error-only). Classified as VISIBLY degraded rather than silently degraded.

other_stubs_in_file.m6_returns: If to_name has any callers: [{"depth": 1, "chain": f"{from_name} → {to_name}"}] (FABRICATED direct path — never verifies from_name actually calls to_name). Else [{"info": "no path found"}].
other_stubs_in_file.pre_m7_behavior: Two-layer: v2_shadow_find_call_path (v2_shadow_adapters.py L817-887) does real BFS shortest-path search over call/indirect/fp_assign edges between from_usrs and to_usrs (up to 5 paths, dedup by chain text). Legacy callgraph.find_call_path uses index_db.find_call_path BFS.
other_stubs_in_file.detail: DANGEROUS stub: it FABRICATES a depth-1 chain 'from_name → to_name' whenever to_name has ANY caller, without verifying that from_name is among them. The returned {depth, chain} shape matches a real call-path result, so a caller would trust a fabricated path that may not exist. The legacy/v2 BFS (with proven endpoints, cycle guard, max_depth, chain dedup) is entirely bypassed. This is worse than an empty return — it returns plausible-but-fake data.

other_stubs_in_file.m6_returns: Delegates to m6_find_indirect_call_sites — returns WHERE a function pointer is INVOKED, not WHICH FUNCTIONS are ASSIGNED to the field.
other_stubs_in_file.pre_m7_behavior: Two-layer: v2_shadow_find_indirect_targets (v2_shadow_adapters.py L1183+) reads `fp_assign` edges and resolves RHS functions assigned to the function-pointer field (rhs_name/rhs_qname/fn_ptr_type/assign_file/assign_line/call_file/call_line/method). Legacy find_indirect_targets links assignment sites to call sites via the field's USR.
other_stubs_in_file.detail: Returns the WRONG query's results. find_indirect_call_sites answers 'where is this function pointer invoked?'; find_indirect_targets should answer 'which functions are assigned to this function-pointer field?'. The return shape (file/line/expr_text of call sites) differs from the expected shape (rhs_name/rhs_qname/assign_file/assign_line/call_file/call_line/method). A caller would get call-site data mislabeled as assignment-target data.

other_stubs_in_file.m6_returns: {"symbol": symbol, "groups": [], "unobserved": []}  — hardcoded, never touches the M6 store.
other_stubs_in_file.pre_m7_behavior: Legacy mcp__fw_context__group_equivalent_variants groups builds by the observed behavior fingerprint of one symbol (SHA-256 over normalized signature + ifdef-filtered body tokens + sorted confirmed outgoing call edges), returning groups with variants/config_hashes/builds and an unobserved list.
other_stubs_in_file.detail: Returns empty groups and empty unobserved. A caller concludes 'no equivalent variants / symbol not observed in any build' when the M6 adapter never computed fingerprints or grouped builds. The empty-groups shape is indistinguishable from a legitimate 'this symbol has no equivalent variants' answer.

partial_degradations_note: Beyond the pure stubs above, several M6 adapters return REAL but SIMPLIFIED data (not pure stubs): m6_semantic_search (L56-59) and m6_smart_search (L62-65) delegate to search_code (no embeddings/LLM pipeline); m6_find_all_callers_recursive (L70-73) is depth-1 only, not recursive; m6_find_callees_recursive (L85-104) is not recursive; m6_find_wrapper_callers (L173-176) does not perform wrapper-class detection; m6_get_inheritance_chain (L230-240) populates bases only (no derived) and calls project_build_kind twice. These return real store data but with reduced fidelity vs the legacy contract. They are degradations, not silent stubs.

summary.verdict: ALL 6 target adapters are stubs returning hardcoded values with no M6 store access and no backing m6_query primitive. 5 of 6 are SILENTLY degraded (return shape mimics a legitimate empty/no-result answer). compare_variants is the exception — it includes an explicit error key (visibly degraded). 3 additional stubs were found elsewhere in the file, including find_call_path which FABRICATES plausible-but-fake call paths. No target adapter is functionally equivalent to its pre-M7 baseline.
